Make sure you've scrubbed out the tub first if it's dirt ( no duh), and scrub it out again when you've finished all the washing because some detergent/color residues can irritate the skin or stain the tub. You need to wash with detergent first, wring everything out as much as possible, drain the tub, then rinse and wring out again. You may want to get some heavy duty dish gloves to do more than one load, because a lot of laundry soaps contain stuff that will irritate your hands, especially when you're rubbing wet fabric & wringing stuff out constantly. Jeans are a b*tch to wash by hand, btw. For cottons/sheets/towels, twisting and wringing them out works pretty well. With sheets you can gently twist them, then double them up creating a twisted sheet-rope type thing, which you loop that over something like a shortened broom/mop handle, or clean stick/ pipe) in order to better be able to twist/wring out more fabric at once over the tub. For more delicate things: gently squeeze out some of the water (do not twist/wring them) , lay the clothes on a dry towel laid out flat, then roll the towel up with the clothes inside (like a jellyroll cake ) and gently twist the towel to get out enough excess water to put in the dryer or hang dry. And give yourself (an your back) a break : wash things like underwear, bras, socks, lightwight/silk blouses ect. in a regular sink instead of the tub-- it's easier to see what needs extra scrubbing and take care of more delicate items.

Good luck, it's exhausting work on a long term basis!
